report:
Erhaltene Artikulation im rechten Kniegelenk. Als anatomische Normvariante Patella tripartita am superolateralen Pol (4/7) mit geringem Knochenmarködem in dem kleinerem akzessorischen Fragment (4/7). Ansonsten altersentsprechendes Knochenmarkssignal.

Patella zentriert stehend. Mehrere oberflächliche, teils bis zur Hälfte der Knorpelschicht erreichenden chondralen Läsionen (siehe z. B. 7/9). Chondrale Calcinosis femoropatellar, führend retropatellar (z. B. 3/46 und 3/57). Ansonsten erhaltene Knorpelbelag.

Femorotibial lateralseitig erhaltener Knorpelbelag ohne tief greifende Chondropathie jedoch mit auffallender chondraler Calcinosis (z. B. 4/25). Der Außenmeniskus ist intakt.

Medialseitig teils fokal tief greifende Chondropathie (z. B. 6/10 oder 4/23) in der Hauptbelastungszone der Femurkondyle. Ansonsten vorwiegend oberflächliche Chondropathie. Hier nur sehr geringe Chondrokalzinose. Der Innenmeniskus ab Pars intermedia bis ins Hinterhorn deutlich signalalteriert und aufgetrieben mit schräger Risskomponente (z. B. 5/9) und kleiner meniscealer Zyste (4/19). Diskrete osteophytäre Anbauten (1005/73).

Vorderes und hinteres Kreuzband intakt. Kollateralbänder intakt, geringer Reizzustand des MCL. Geringer Gelenkerguss. Synovialis nicht verdickt. Vergrößerte Bursa praepatellaris (5/20). Ansonsten unauffällige Darstellung der umgebenden Muskulatur und der Subkutis.

Ekstensör mekanizma bunların dışında korunmuş (kuadriseps tendonu ve patellar tendon, patella ve yerleşimi, femoral troklear oluk ve patellofemoral bağlar normal). Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı normal. Gastroknemyus-semimembranozus bursasındaki küçük sıvı koleksiyonu sızdırmıyor. Posteromedyal parakapsüler ödem hafif derecede. Çapraz ve yan bağlar normal. Medyal menisküs normal. Lateral menisküsün korpus kesiminde serbest kenarda püsküllenme olabilir.

There is mild soft tissue swelling along anterior medial and lateral aspect of the knee.  
 Bone contusion at anterior lateral femoral condyle and posterior lateral  and  medial proximal tibia is noted. 
    Hyperintense disrupted mid to proximal ACL is detected.   Buckling PCL with intact ligament is observed.  Anterior tibial translation is noted.     
    Longitudinal vertical tear at posterior horn involved posterior root of the medial meniscus is detected.  Mild hyperintense proximal MCL is seen.      
   Mild hyperintense proximal FCL and popliteus tendon and distal biceps femoris tendon are noted.    Lateral meniscus is not torn.   
   Focal partial thickness cartilage loss at posterior lateral femoral condyle, non weight bearing part, without subchondral bone lesion, is observed. 
   PF joint is preserved.  Medial and lateral retinacula are intact. 
   Quadriceps and patellar tendon are intact.  
   Minimal joint effusion is seen.   -  Complete tear of ACL 
 -  Mild proximal MCL sprain  
 -  Longitudinal vertical tear at posterior horn involved posterior root of the medial meniscus  
 -  Proximal FCL sprain,   
    Popliteus and biceps femoris tendons strain  
 -  Partial thickness cartilage loss at posterior lateral femoral condyle, non weight bearing part,  
    without subchondral bone lesion, chondropathy grade 3.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Minimal left knee joint effusion. Joint effusion. No popliteal cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
There is some focal cartilage thinning, fissuring and irregularity involving the weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle without any associated subchondral bone marrow reactive signal intensity changes.

Normal appearances of the medial collateral ligament and medial meniscus.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
There is some subchondral bone marrow contusion involving the anterolateral aspect of the lateral tibial plateau with subtle low signal intensity subcortical linear abnormality that is most visible on the sagittal PD images.
Depending on the clinical presentation/mechanism of injury this could represent a subtle undisplaced subcortical stress fracture or insufficiency fracture [microtrabecular injury], with associated surrounding contusion.

Morphology of the medial collateral ligament complex and medial meniscus is unremarkable.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Normal.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
There is some focal articular cartilage fissuring of the junction of the median ridge and lateral patellar facet, without subchondral bone marrow reactive signal intensity changes.

Focal thinning and irregularity involving the central and medial trochlear articular cartilage without subchondral bone marrow reactive changes.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
1.No internal derangement of the knee ligaments or menisci is identified.
2.Anterolateral tibial plateau: There is some subchondral bone marrow contusion involving the anterolateral aspect of the lateral tibial plateau with subtle low signal intensity subcortical linear abnormality that is most visible on the sagittal PD images. Depending on the clinical presentation/mechanism of injury this could represent a subtle undisplaced subcortical stress fracture or insufficiency fracture [microtrabecular injury], with associated surrounding contusion. Recommend orthopedic surgery/sports medicine evaluation for recommendation regarding if the patient should be nonweightbearing.
3.Moderate medial compartment and patellofemoral compartment chondrosis, as described.
4.Mild left knee joint effusion.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee pain
Comparison: MRI right knee to [DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No significant joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Cartilage thinning at the periphery of the medial femoral condyle medial tibial plateau. No full-thickness cartilage defect.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Cartilage thinning at the posterior lateral tibial plateau. No full-thickness defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Broad areas of full-thickness cartilage loss extending from the median ridge through the lateral patellar facet with subchondral cystic change. Broad areas of full-thickness cartilage loss along the lateral trochlea with subchondral cystic change. Cartilage heterogeneity and partial-thickness loss along the medial patellar facet and medial trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Medial collateral ligament is intact and normal in appearance. There is a mild MCL bursitis, significantly improved since prior study.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Trace edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Grade 4 patellofemoral compartment chondrosis, mildly progressed along the trochlea since prior study.
2. Mild MCL bursitis, significantly improved since prior study.
3. No meniscal tear or ligamentous injury.

MRI of Left Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS, AX T2W FS


> Mild thickening of quadriceps tendon with increased signal intensity on F/S T2WI, R/O grade 1 injury.
> Linear and blurring hyperintensity in the posterior horn of medial meniscus with articular surface disruption, in favor of longitudinal tear(srs 3001 img4-5)
> Mild increased intensity in the lateral meniscus, in favor intrasubstance degeneration
>The contour of ACL is not all in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, R/O mucoid degenration and partial tear
> There was no abnormal intensity in the PCL
> Wearing articular cartilage of knee joint with large spur formation and tiny subchondral cysts, more severe at medial compartment, reflecting osteoarthritis. 
> Focal increased intensity in the patellar cartilage with fissure and tiny subchondral cyst, more prominent at medial side, in favor of grade 4 chondral injury.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> Subcutaneous infiltration with heterogenous enhancement noted in the prepatellar to infrapatellar region, edematous change 
> A small lobulated cystic lesion in popliteal fossa with a small recess of the knee joint capsule lies medially between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of small Baker's cyst.

Impression:
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee.
2. Synovitis of left knee joint with grade 4 chondromalacia.
3. R/O mucoid degenration and partial tear of AXL. 
4. Subcutanoeus infilammation over prepatellar to infrapatellar region.
5. Degeneration and tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe longitudinal tear.
6. R/O synovial cyst or paramenical cyst in anterior intercondylar region of left knee.
7. Mild Anserine bursitis.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and lab data.

Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Intact.

Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Areas of full-thickness chondral fissuring at the medial patellar facet.

Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 6 mm, normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

2.9 x 1.6 x 1.6 cm multiloculated cystic lesion at the posterolateral knee, likely a ganglion cyst. 1.9 x 0.5 x 0.8 cm multiloculated cyst at the medial joint line. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

3.	Multiloculated ganglion cyst at the medial knee measuring up to 1.9 cm. 
4.	Multiloculated cyst at the posterolateral knee measuring up to 2.9 cm, likely arising from the popliteus tendon sheath.
